lark_e13_entry.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_entry.text: On Day Eighty One, Lin woke in the provider's received lower resting room with the ankle swollen inside its ordinary wrap. The foot had not become ready for a normal stair because she had managed to sleep. She used the temporary crutch only for the short movement the clinician had actually permitted. The longer gallery view remained outside her window, ruined and distant. Today's instruction was rest and current receiving, not an inspection expedition she could justify by claiming that a story needed its injured witness to see everything personally.

lark_e13_entry_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_entry_002.text: The meal arrived under her existing received lodging provision. Its keeper had agreed to bring the bowl to the lower room while her current movement was restricted; there was no unpriced household duty silently placed on Shan Fang. Lin ate slowly and answered the keeper's practical question about where the crutch could stand without narrowing the door. They put it beside the low table. A recovering person's room could become an obstruction if every useful object was left where the last difficult movement had ended.

lark_e13_entry_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_entry_003.text: The ordinary clinic had six current treatment places within its accepted lower rooms. Ke Wen occupied one under his guides' existing care arrangement. Lin's room belonged to her lodging provider, not a seventh bed invented inside the clinic. The staff moved completed simple examinations out of the treatment places as their actual plans allowed. New people waited under the independent shelter's offered counting and seating. The qualified receivers did not tell every hurt person that a reserved place existed before someone had actually checked its current capacity.

lark_e13_entry_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_entry_004.text: Ke Wen's sister reached the clinic by the presently open lower road on Day Eighty Two. The receiving keeper confirmed her actual arrival to the guide before admitting her to his offered patient place. She had been told about the permanent removal of the crushed lower arm, not promised a limb waiting whole beneath a dressing. Lin learned the news through the guide's permitted message. The sister's name was Ke Lan, and her ordinary arrival supplied family company. It did not supply a new surgeon or make the wound's course less necessary.

lark_e13_entry_005.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_entry_005.text: Zhou Min visited Lin's lower room after closing the current tally account with its qualified receiver. The missing names had been traced through actual receiving wherever the routes allowed. One traveller had gone down the lower coach road before the warning and had never entered the gallery group. Another remained an unresolved current question because the last offered route had no returned message yet. Zhou Min would not combine them into a dramatic count of deaths or a reassuring count of all safe. Each name needed its own actual source.

lark_e13_entry_006.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_entry_006.text: The qualified ground crew kept the damaged upper bays closed. The first later inspection would take place only after current movement allowed a controlled approach within a newly received plan. Merchants wanted their cargo counted immediately. The crew could receive those lists at the lower desk without sending someone across unstable debris to satisfy them. Lin heard the ordinary limit from the keeper who brought today's public notice. The old spent timber and notices had reduced confusion before the fall; their purchase did not buy safe footing after it.

lark_e13_entry_007.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_entry_007.text: Qin had lost two future bookings when their cargo disappeared beneath the closed bay. He had completed neither delivery and received no completed work fee for them. Their actual cancellation terms would be handled by the freight receivers, not paid from Lin's instruction place. He came to her room with a smaller bundle of ordinary household news than usual. The cart was intact because it had been at home after its completed lower job. That survival did not turn his missing future work into a hidden profit.

lark_e13_entry_008.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_entry_008.text: Shan Fang's neighbors had eight offered winter glove pattern jobs waiting at five copper each after actual completed receiving. Those offers required the shared working patterns, besides private measurements kept elsewhere. Whether the consented packet had survived would now change which work they could honestly accept. The forty copper was a possible livelihood, not cash already lost or earned. Lin had helped at one actual post. The later verified inventory would determine what existed for the neighbors and what existed for the apparatus crew, without taking every useful object from a different possible morning.

lark_e13_entry_009.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_entry_009.text: On Day Eighty Four, the qualified crew released a narrow controlled ground inspection after the new movement checks. Its team received the current route and returned with actual fragments, marked locations, and the stock it could safely recover. No one claimed that an empty spot seen through dust established permanent destruction. The survivors' records and damaged cases were compared with their keepers' receiving lists. Lin remained in her lower room. The keeper brought the report there so she could receive its facts without walking on the injured ankle to earn the right to know them.

lark_e13_entry_010.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_entry_010.text: The report distinguished three unique working objects whose custody had been near the warning posts: the relay's contemporaneous operating log, the neighbors' consented pattern packet, and the hardware crew's brass timing comb. Their safe receiving and the recovered damage now had actual evidence behind them. One post had received Lin's ordinary help and light case custody. The other posts had prioritized people under their actual withdrawal. The report would show those particular results, leaving Lin's unchanged past stage certificate irrelevant to which object had physically reached the refuge.

lark_e13_stock_gate.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_stock_gate.text: The keeper read the verified stock report beside the actual warning post receiving. A saved log, saved pattern packet, and saved timing comb would support different future work; damaged missing objects would not be declared restored because one useful case arrived. Where a prior assignment had no received custody, the new report would retain that gap without manufacturing a selected rescue.

lark_e13_log_001.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_log_001.text: Jiang's current operating log had reached the shelter under the accepted relay custody. The qualified keeper compared the surviving sequence with the lower receiver's warning message and retained both as real sources. The detailed page could show the bed's measured condition at the last powered warning and the isolation that followed. It could not show every person who heard the bell. Later reconstruction would begin with an actual local timing record instead of inventing one from the loudness people remembered through rain and fear.

lark_e13_log_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_log_002.text: The log's presence allowed the operator to separate a tested external fuel discharge from the later bed failure. Jiang could name which checks had been performed before the accepted warning and which conditions changed afterward. That distinction would help the inquiry ask the right structural question rather than accuse every signal of causing what it announced. It did not settle every cause of the moving slope. The report promised evidence for a bounded apparatus history, which was valuable precisely because its page did not pretend to contain the whole mountain.

lark_e13_log_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_log_003.text: Shan Fang's permitted packet had not survived. She had put it down under the lane's required human withdrawal when Ke Wen's injured arm needed ordinary support. The recovered outer fold and ruined pages were identified at the released inspection, their ink dispersed through wet debris. Private customer measurements had stayed elsewhere, but the complex consented repair patterns themselves were no longer usable. The owners could remember parts of their work. They could not honestly reconstruct every shape and dimension as if memory were another intact copy hidden under the room's shelf.

lark_e13_log_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_log_004.text: The neighbors withdrew the eight pattern dependent offers before accepting deposits or sending false completion dates. Forty copper in possible work would now be earned elsewhere by people who had the required method and materials. Shan Fang could still take ordinary repairs whose tasks she knew without those pages. She accepted two such smaller jobs under their actual terms. The change reduced the coming season's income and narrowed its work. Lin heard the numbers from the owners, not as a fictional loss she could cancel by making the surviving log more important.

lark_e13_log_005.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_log_005.text: Mao Ren's brass timing comb was recovered in broken pieces from the damaged station. Its original calibrated sequence could no longer be used; two marked arms had split and several working teeth were missing. The private dimensions were not fully recorded in an available intact source. Welding the fragments together would not restore its received rating. The crew would need a fresh calibration project or a simpler slower method. It chose to plan a conservative sequential closure comparison before accepting another two turn operation that depended on the lost original.

lark_e13_log_006.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_log_006.text: That choice would permit only one received freight turn in the corresponding future work period until a different method earned its own rating. Carriers could not charge the association for two completed turns while only one existed. Qin expected fewer suitable bookings and began asking about independent lower road work. The limit was not a punishment for saving the log. It followed from the missing hardware comparison. A useful record could support a careful inquiry and still leave people with a physically smaller working system afterward.

lark_e13_log_007.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_log_007.text: Jiang asked Lin for the ordinary custody acknowledgment she had signed at the shelter. She offered the receiving line and the isolated message she had actually carried. He did not ask her to claim she had watched the lane injury or hardware shutdown. The inquiry could use his contemporaneous log alongside their qualified reports. Lin felt grateful to have preserved something useful and guilty about the other owners' losses. Neither feeling changed the assignment she had accepted or gave her a second withdrawal path through the completed event.

lark_e13_log_008.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_log_008.text: Shan Fang thanked her for the help that had actually warned the group, without thanking her for pages she had not carried. Their next mending gathering would use different work and smaller offers. Lin asked whether she could help prepare permitted new examples later, after ordinary recovery. Shan Fang said they could discuss an actual new task then. A future project might be worthwhile, but it would not be the old packet recovered in disguise. The closed loss made the promise of new work more honest, and no less difficult.

lark_e13_log_009.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_log_009.text: The keeper received the surviving log, the destroyed packet, and the unusable comb as separate outcomes. Later apparatus review had a precise history; the neighbors had lost complex patterns; the crew had lost its original sequence comparison. No transfer between those statements could repay the people whose methods were gone. Lin filed the report beside her actual relay receiving and kept the ankle raised as instructed. She had one useful case in the right cupboard and a mountain whose other missing stock would now alter real lives.

lark_e13_patterns_001.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_patterns_001.text: The packet's owners received their intact consented patterns from the shelter cupboard and checked each against the offered stock list. Its ordinary waxed fold had been packed for walking, and Lin's accepted lane custody had kept it within a permitted low load. The private customer measurements had stayed elsewhere and could now be compared by their actual keeper. The packet would let the neighbors decide on the eight winter jobs from real available methods. It was not a spiritual inheritance whose rescue granted Lin rights over anybody else's labor.

lark_e13_patterns_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_patterns_002.text: Shan Fang and the other owner accepted the eight five copper offers under actual completion dates and material scopes. Two ordinary repairs were completed and received by Day Eighty Six, paying ten copper to the people who did that work. Six remained ahead, with thirty copper possible only after their own receiving. Lin earned none of this household income by having carried the packet. The consented stock had preserved a practical opportunity for other people's skilled hands. Those hands still had to cut, stitch, fit, and deliver every promised glove.

lark_e13_patterns_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_patterns_003.text: Jiang's detailed operating case had been left under the relay's required withdrawal when the bed's failed condition demanded the operator's hands and attention. The controlled later inspection received its crushed lid and dispersed working pages. The lower warning message survived, giving the issued instruction and its receiving time. The finer sequence of local fuel and condition checks was gone. The operator could offer what he remembered and the qualified current reports that remained. He could not create a contemporaneous log afterward and ask the inquiry to treat it as the missing original.

lark_e13_patterns_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_patterns_004.text: The review would therefore retain uncertainty about parts of that bed history. Its later safe replacement could be tested under new conditions, but those tests would not prove every value from the destroyed morning. The association refused to publish a clean exact sequence assembled from approximate recollections. It planned additional current calibration before any comparable operation. The saved repair patterns gave no shortcut to that engineering work. They had supported a different livelihood, whose usefulness could remain clear beside an unanswered technical question.

lark_e13_patterns_005.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_patterns_005.text: Mao Ren's original brass timing comb had also been destroyed. The controlled inspection recovered split marked arms and missing working teeth, enough to identify the object without restoring its rating. Its full calibrated dimensions had no intact permitted duplicate. The crew would not weld an attractive outline and call it the original working comparison. It planned a slower sequential closure method that could be tested independently. Until that method earned more, the related future work period would take one received freight turn instead of two.

lark_e13_patterns_006.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_patterns_006.text: Qin read that practical limit beside his possible jobs. He could not base next month's household income on a second turn whose comparison system no longer existed. The pattern work had preserved Shan Fang's offers, while his own suitable freight opportunities narrowed. They planned the season with both facts instead of arguing which object would have made the family universally better off. Lin had helped the walking group and brought one packet through its actual route. The other lost tools would still change the household's money and hours.

lark_e13_patterns_007.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_patterns_007.text: The inquiry asked Lin for her ordinary lane custody and the injury she had actually witnessed. She could identify the packet transfer and Ke Wen's damaged arm at the marker. She could not describe the relay bed's last external strip from a place she had not stood. Jiang's current warning message and qualified account would supply the facts available there. The missing detailed log was not secretly inside her memory because she understood why it would have been useful. Every source remained tied to its actual observer and time.

lark_e13_patterns_008.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_patterns_008.text: Shan Fang said the packet's survival mattered more than she had been willing to admit during the preparation meeting. She had avoided asking Lin to promise it, because the human withdrawal came first. Now she could be glad of a real saved livelihood without pretending her choice would have been the only right one for everyone. Lin asked how the first received jobs had gone. One glove needed a seam taken down and redone before the owner accepted it. Ordinary work had resumed with an ordinary correction, rather than with a triumphant perfect week.

lark_e13_patterns_009.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_patterns_009.text: The keeper received the preserved patterns, destroyed detailed log, and unusable comb as different outcomes. The neighbors had a working method and actual new income, while the apparatus review had less evidence and the crew a smaller planned operation. Lin put that report beside her lane receiving. She was glad about the packet, shaken by the guide's permanent injury, and unable to make either result replace the other. Her raised ankle would still need its own current reassessment before a life with this changed stock could begin moving again.

lark_e13_comb_001.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_comb_001.text: Mao Ren's brass timing comb survived in the case Lin had received after the qualified shutdown. Its original marks and teeth matched the crew's current stock list, and its ordinary dry custody at the shelter kept the calibration source usable. The keeper did not install it into damaged hardware immediately. The comb could support later tested reconstruction, not prove the ruined station safe by being laid beside it. Lin's narrow recorder work had preserved a unique tool for other people's qualified hands, under rights that remained with its owner.

lark_e13_comb_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_comb_002.text: The crew could plan a later two turn comparison project instead of beginning with a lost sequence and a conservative one turn substitute. Actual operation would still require a new grounded board, current structural rating, qualified operators, and received tests. The intact comb shortened one part of that work without creating timber or unpriced labor. Qin read the proposed capacity beside his future bookings and waited for an actual approval before accepting two deliveries. A saved tool had preserved a practical possibility that was not yet completed income.

lark_e13_comb_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_comb_003.text: Jiang's detailed operating case had not reached the shelter. The later controlled inspection received its crushed cover and dispersed timing pages under an identified location. The lower receiver's warning message survived, but the finer bed history was gone. Jiang could offer his actual recollection and current qualified reports. He could not make a new page into the destroyed contemporaneous sequence merely by writing carefully. The inquiry would have to keep that missing evidence visible while establishing the warning facts its remaining sources could support.

lark_e13_comb_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_comb_004.text: Additional current calibration would be needed before a comparable replacement bed could be received. Those new tests could establish a safe future task. They could not determine every exact value from the lost morning. The surviving hardware comb answered a different question. The association refused the convenient story in which any intact technical object became proof that every system had operated exactly as intended. Lin heard the plan from its actual keeper and understood why her useful case could not make the review's missing page less missing.

lark_e13_comb_005.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_comb_005.text: Shan Fang's consented pattern packet had been left under the lane's human withdrawal when the wounded guide needed ordinary support. Its identified fold and ink dispersed pages came back from the controlled inspection. Private customer measurements remained in their separate custody, but the complex shared patterns were no longer usable. The owners could remember parts of them and had no intact hidden copy of every shape. Lin would not offer to recreate the full stock from the handful of examples she had seen during household evenings.

lark_e13_comb_006.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_comb_006.text: The owners withdrew the eight pattern dependent glove offers before accepting deposits or false delivery dates. Forty copper in possible work went to other makers who had the needed method and materials. Shan Fang could still take ordinary repairs whose tasks she knew independently, and accepted two smaller ones. The lost pattern stock narrowed her season's livelihood even while the comb preserved a possible future freight capacity. Qin and Shan Fang planned with that uneven result instead of pretending a household could be saved entirely by one tool in a dry cupboard.

lark_e13_comb_007.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_comb_007.text: The inquiry asked Lin for the shutdown message and timing case custody she had actually received. She could identify the operator's statement, the visible closed indication, and the ordinary handoff. She could not claim to have observed Ke Wen's impact or the bed's last external strip. Their actual witnesses would give their own accounts, with the missing log honestly marked. Her recorder's useful precision mattered because it stayed narrow. A person who had carried one case did not become the author of every source the mountain had destroyed.

lark_e13_comb_008.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_comb_008.text: Mao Ren thanked her for preserving the comparison and asked whether its low case had strained the recovering shoulder. She reported the actual carry and new ankle injury. He did not treat the useful tool as compensation for her body's cost. He would use its owner received stock under the later reconstruction scope, with Lin invited to observe only if a new permitted appointment and her ordinary recovery allowed it. The thanks closed an actual volunteer task. It did not buy future unpriced labor from the person who had made the handoff possible.

lark_e13_comb_009.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_comb_009.text: The keeper received the intact comb, destroyed detailed log, and lost pattern stock as different outcomes. The crew retained a unique comparison, the apparatus review had less exact history, and the neighbors had lost work they could no longer honestly offer. Lin filed the report beside her ground station receiving and rested the ankle. The case's real usefulness would matter again when rebuilding began. It would not regrow the guide's missing hand or tell the winter glove owners that another household's preserved opportunity paid for the one they had lost.

lark_e13_room_001.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_room_001.text: The inventory's different outcomes would remain attached to their actual receiving. Lin could not pay a guide's medical cost with a better technical explanation, or reimburse a lost winter job with a saved case whose owner had different work. She read the report once more, then let the keeper take it to the next actual receiver. Her lower room was not the whole association's office. The ankle needed its protected position while other people carried the work she could presently hear about but not perform.

lark_e13_room_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_room_002.text: The clinic's current account showed sixty copper in the guides' received seasonal care subscriptions. Twenty eight had paid Ke Wen's accepted operation, immediate ordinary materials, and received early treatment scope; thirty two remained for later agreed care. It was a finite mutual arrangement, not the weather watch's notice purse or Lin's personal appropriation. Ke Lan read the actual remaining scope with its keeper. She would need to plan ordinary food, lodging, and any later support around what the family and fund could truly receive. A missing hand had not been bought back for any amount.

lark_e13_room_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_room_003.text: Ke Lan had brought a shirt that buttoned awkwardly for a person using one hand. The clinic receiver asked whether she wanted it altered and directed the request to a known ordinary mender. Shan Fang could perform that small alteration independently of the lost or surviving complex pattern stock. She accepted its actual price and delivered the changed fastening after receiving the sleeve's private dimensions under their limited permission. The useful work did not remake the absent forearm. It made one daily task less dependent on somebody always standing at Ke Wen's elbow.

lark_e13_room_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_room_004.text: Ke Wen began to wake more clearly on Day Eighty Three. His ordinary wound plan still required dressings, protected movement, and current monitoring; clarity was not recovery completed. He asked Ke Lan to place the familiar keys where his right hand could find them. The left side of his body still seemed to expect a hand at its old distance. The clinic explained that feeling without calling it proof the limb was secretly returning. He could reach the key ring with the hand that remained and fail to close fingers that no longer existed.

lark_e13_room_005.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_room_005.text: Zhou Min gave him the finished current tally with the unresolved name finally answered by an actual receiving from farther down the lower road. He listened, asked about one family's returned count, and corrected a doubled household line. His guiding knowledge had not been crushed along with the arm. He was not presently fit for a full route watch, and the tally correction did not change that. The receiver thanked him for the small competent contribution and let him rest. Useful work could resume in a limited form without requiring the injured person to pretend the loss had become trivial.

lark_e13_room_006.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_room_006.text: Lin heard the correction through Ke Wen's permitted message and wanted to see him. The clinician kept her protected rest plan and offered a short seated meeting only if the guide's own current transfer was accepted. Ke Wen asked to come to her lower doorway on Day Eighty Five with Ke Lan, within his ordinary plan. The route crossed the clear courtyard and no damaged gallery stair. The clinic receiver received his tolerated condition before the visit. Two hurt people could meet without treating either one's desire for company as authority to disregard the other's body.

lark_e13_room_007.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_room_007.text: He sat in the supported chair beside her door and said the paper shoe had probably performed better than both of them. Lin told him it had done no work at all. He seemed pleased by the answer. They spoke first about the guide's father's tune and the way its ornament hid the freight rhythm. Ke Wen's left sleeve rested closed against the new dressing. His right hand moved as he described a phrase, then stopped when he reached for the absent second grip. He looked at the hand he had and said nothing for a while.

lark_e13_room_008.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_room_008.text: Lin did not tell him he would certainly find a way to play the same double flute. Its holes required the hand he had lost, and any changed instrument would need its own making and learning. He said people had already offered versions of that reassurance. They wanted him to remain the familiar person quickly enough that their memories would not hurt. Lin asked whether he wanted the flute brought from home now or left there. He wanted it brought, closed in its ordinary cloth, so the choice to touch it would remain his.

lark_e13_room_009.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_room_009.text: Ke Lan said she would bring it after checking that it had not been damaged at home. The current independent building remained usable, but the family still inspected actual things rather than finding safety in a broad adjective. Ke Wen asked Lin whether the ankle would let her climb by next week. She said the current plan did not promise it. He nodded and told her not to turn a small injured foot into a competition with his arm. The warning was kinder than an invitation to ignore her own pain because his looked worse.

lark_e13_room_010.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_room_010.text: He had no appetite for being called the person who sacrificed an arm to save everybody. He had taken an ordinary position at a marker and been hit by stone while doing a qualified job. The people had been withdrawing through a prepared route. That fact mattered, and it did not make his injury a chosen payment for their lives. Lin understood why the grander story could be cruel. It asked him to consent afterward to the loss so everyone else could regard the morning as orderly.

lark_e13_room_011.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_room_011.text: The clinic receiver ended the visit within its accepted time. Ke Wen returned across the courtyard with his sister under the same ordinary plan, without carrying a grateful guest or proving a longer walk. Lin kept the ankle supported after the door closed. The meeting had helped and tired her. Its actual price was a quiet hour afterward, not an unspoken duty to become his permanent listener. Ke Lan sent word that he had reached the patient place comfortably enough. Lin received the small source and was glad of its modest certainty.

lark_e13_room_012.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_room_012.text: The ordinary desk keeper brought the current care cover receiving on Day Eighty Six. Two qualified replacement sessions, on Days Eighty Three and Eighty Six, had performed work Lin could not take while the ankle required protected rest. Five copper each came from the twenty copper qualified cover portion, leaving ten. Lin had received no completed shift wages for those two canceled personal dates. The keeper could later offer new actual desk tasks within the remaining term, but their wages would depend on her return conditions and completed receiving.

lark_e13_room_013.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_room_013.text: She disliked seeing another person's name where hers had been pencilled. The replacement was necessary, accepted, and paid for the work it did. Disliking it did not make the replacement less competent or the care allowance a favor she had to repay with premature walking. The keeper showed which continuing desk tasks remained in the term and asked her to review them only after the clinician received a return plan. Lin put the offered dates aside. The page was evidence of a livelihood still possible, not pressure to perform it from a bed.

lark_e13_room_014.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_room_014.text: Her fifth ordinary assessment was received that afternoon. Five copper paid the clinician's current examination, bringing the assessment portion to twenty five spent and fifteen still available. The ankle remained swollen under a load that changed her gait. Protected rest would continue through the initial fourteen days after the injury, Days Eighty One through Ninety Four, with the ordinary plan reviewed before any increase. The clinician stopped both primary leg tasks and the untested lateral lower limb sixth pair preparation. The fifth upper limb practice remained paused while her whole recovery condition was unsettled.

lark_e13_room_015.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_room_015.text: The current four pair certificate remained the past recovered result it had actually established. Its present usable scope was smaller because a leg movement was injured. Duan received that distinction beside the ordinary care report and did not test Lin's reserve to argue the tissue into compliance. His next formal teaching meeting would be unpowered explanation and current source reading within its accepted scope, if she felt able to take it. No lesson was performed merely because a patient wanted the fee plan to feel productive. She would answer on the actual appointment date.

lark_e13_room_016.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_room_016.text: Shan Fang brought an ordinary sleeve basket for her own mending while visiting. Lin did not need to furnish another subject to keep her there. The two women worked and rested side by side, with the actual needle task in Shan Fang's hands. Qin Yi had been quieter since the shelter and asked before touching the little paper shoe on Lin's table. Lin let her inspect its curled edge. The child said it looked older now. Her mother did not insist the child make the joke cheerful.

lark_e13_room_017.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_room_017.text: Qin Yi wanted to know whether Ke Wen's missing hand would return if he became a powerful cultivator. Lin gave the bounded answer she knew: the stages and current methods they were working with did not promise regrowth, and Ke Wen's ordinary treatment had received a permanent loss. She did not invent a distant realm as a consolation the child could expect them to reach. Qin Yi asked whether a new flute would have fewer holes. That was a real craft question they could put to a maker later, with the guide's actual consent.

lark_e13_room_018.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_room_018.text: The child's question stayed open. Ke Lan brought the old flute from the inspected home and placed it beside the guide's patient belongings, under his offered permission. He did not play it that day. He unwrapped it with the right hand and ran a finger over the worn holes. Zhou Min told Lin about the actual receiving afterward, because Ke Wen had agreed the small news could be shared. An old instrument could remain part of a life without being forced to demonstrate that the life had already adapted.

lark_e13_room_019.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_room_019.text: Qin brought his canceled booking accounts after their freight receivers had closed the scope. The paid waiting and cancellation sums came from the actual offered terms, not a universal courier rule. Neither account paid him for a completed load he had not delivered. He was seeking ordinary work on the lower road with its present inspection and different receiving places. Lin could read the offered papers when her current fatigue allowed it. She could not accept the jobs for him or make the lower road preserve every profitable habit of the gallery.

lark_e13_room_020.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_room_020.text: The jar seller's losses were confirmed through the controlled cargo inspection. Broken pottery and spoiled contents could be counted where the new safe route allowed, while unreachable stock stayed unresolved instead of being called intact. The seller had enough surviving jars for a smaller ordinary stall and no reason to celebrate the reduced rent as profit. She sent a permitted note to Lin thanking the notice writer whose clear closure had stopped her assistant returning for a crate. The assistant's survival had been useful and real; the missing winter earnings were also useful and real.

lark_e13_room_021.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_room_021.text: At the lower receiving table, the association planned the inquiry's first seated witness session for Day Eighty Seven. It would use the actual surviving records and receive recollections under their limits. Lin's prior supplier statement choice had created a public paid statement, a keeper held observer file, or neither new account. Those outcomes would determine what the inquiry could ask her to bring and what later readers could examine. The current request would not turn an absent detailed report into a paper she had secretly written.

lark_e13_room_022.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_room_022.text: Hu Lan asked whether Lin could give a seated current account within her ordinary recovery plan. The clinician allowed a short received interval in the lower room, with the ankle supported and no walking inspection added. Lin accepted that limited appearance. It would not be unpaid freight work or an opportunity to complete the failed technical recruitment. She would give what she had actually seen, source what others had told her, and mark what remained unknown. The offer sounded modest before she imagined people asking for a clean cause of an event that had taken a hand.

lark_e13_room_023.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_room_023.text: She read the public supplier notice that was available under its actual source, then the ordinary current withdrawal record from her own post. The remade joint had been carried away on Day Seventy Nine; it had never been installed on the freight bell. That common public fact could answer one false rumor regardless of her earlier signature. The bed's exact timing, where available, answered a different question. The destroyed objects would leave gaps where they had actually been destroyed. Lin would not use one true statement to erase every harder unanswered one.

lark_e13_room_024.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_room_024.text: That evening, the lodging keeper brought the eighth received meal and room week within the continuing twenty four week scope. Forty copper had now been received in that category, with sixteen weeks remaining. The damaged gallery did not make an already received safe room imaginary, nor did it extend the term beyond its accepted end. Lin ate the ordinary bowl and thanked the person whose current task supplied it. The next investigation would need measured words. Tonight's recovery needed food, a quiet door, and the ankle kept where it did not insist on another story.

lark_e13_room_025.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_room_025.text: Before sleeping, she sealed the letter to her mother with the actual current injury and care account. The licensed carrier would accept it when the present ordinary route and dispatch offered a receiving. Lin kept enough of her own money for that post instead of expecting the weather appropriation to carry private news. The letter did not tell her mother that nothing important had been lost. It told her that people were alive, hurt, and beginning work from smaller stocks, and that Lin was resting inside an ordinary plan she meant to keep.

lark_e13_room_026.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_room_026.text: The paper shoe remained on the low table. Ke Wen's old flute remained under his own custody, unplayed. A changed stock report stood in the association file, with different useful evidence and opportunities depending on the actual receiving. None of those things could be simplified into a victorious morning. Lin let them occupy their separate places while sleep approached. She had helped at one post and been injured at one shared step. The next day would ask for a witness, and a witness did not have to become the mountain's author.

lark_e13_table.speaker: narrator
lark_e13_table.text: The inquiry keeper brought a low writing table to the room before fixing tomorrow's witness place. Lin tried its ordinary position with the ankle supported and found that reaching its far edge would make her lean painfully. The keeper moved the table instead of asking her to prove she could sit through inconvenience. The current appearance would receive words, not endurance. Lin marked the useful chair position for the receiver's morning check.
